title: Cross-Area Journey
description: One file per journey at specs/journeys/<slug>.journey.json. A journey is THE use-case mechanism: a named user-visible flow, steps referencing requirement IDs in qualified <area>.<ID> form, in temporal order. Most journeys live inside one area (a 'login' flow over auth alone is a normal journey); some cross boundaries — same shape either way. Same overlay discipline as change manifests: references only, never content — the requirements stay in their area JSONs; delete every journey and the specs are complete. Born at capture time in both directions: in greenfield elicitation one story told = one journey; in brownfield the flow is deduced from the call graph during extraction, one journey per reachable entry point, updated (not duplicated) on re-extraction. EXECUTABLE: `run` names the Quint run that walks the flow end to end (checked by `quint test`, and replayed against code like any example); spec-lint checks that the run calls each step's action in the journey's order. Each step carries its example rows (`examples`, or every example whose @refs names the step), which is what the readback shows at that step.

name.description: Short flow name, e.g. 'Sign up and buy'. Unique across journeys.

description.description: One line: what the actor accomplishes end to end.

run.description: The Quint `run` that walks this journey end to end, qualified <area>.<runName>. It must call the action of every step specified in that area, in this journey's order (spec-lint `journey-run-order`); steps in other areas are covered only through qualified calls (`auth::login(..)`), which needs a model that imports them. Without a run the journey is a picture of a flow rather than a checked one (`journey-not-executable`).

steps.description: Temporal order — this order IS the render order in readbacks. Happy-path step followed immediately by its unwanted counterparts.

ref.description: Qualified requirement reference, <area>.<ID> — same form as cross_refs. A NAV-NNN navigation edge is a valid step too: 'opens Settings from the sidebar' is a step of the flow, not a requirement to invent.

note.description: Optional gloss for the step in journey context, e.g. 'payment declined counterpart'.

examples.description: Qualified example ids (<area>.EX-NNN) shown as Given/When/Then rows at this step. Optional: without it the step shows every example whose @refs names the step's requirement. Each example should exercise the step's own action (`journey-example-off-step`).
